````text
# #4786: Patch: `play_ai_turn` called twice on one game gives every action a nonce the game has not seen
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`play_ai_turn` (`crates/ai/src/match_.rs:488`) numbers its actions `t0, t1, …` from 0 on every call. The engine answers an action whose nonce is already in `state.applied` (the last `NONCE_HISTORY`, 64) as a replay: the state comes back unchanged with `error: None` (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs`, the nonce check). So a second `play_ai_turn` on the state a first one left has its first decisions swallowed: each costs a full `decide`, changes nothing, and is still pushed onto `actions` and `decisions` as if it had been played, because the loop stops only on an error.

Example: p1's turn through `play_ai_turn` applies `t0` (a play) and `t1` (End turn). `play_ai_turn(&first.state, P2, …)` then returns four actions: `t0` and `t1` are the same play of `c6`, answered as replays of p1's nonces, then `t2` (the play, now applied) and `t3` (End turn). A turn that follows a k-action turn loses its first k decisions and that much of its `AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS` ceiling.

Only tests and puzzles call the function today, each once per game, so no shipped game is affected. It is a trap for the next test that plays two turns with it: its `actions` would not be what was played.

### What should happen

Every action `play_ai_turn` returns is one the engine applied (`crates/ai/README.md`, Matches: "`play_ai_turn` plays one AI turn out"). `play_match` already avoids the clash with `m{log.len()}`.

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7). Also on branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`, `crates/ai/tests/audit_decks.rs`.

```rust
use jackioh_ai::{AI_GATE_BUDGET, AiOptions, play_ai_turn};
use jackioh_engine::testkit::{Action, PlayerId, create_rng, hash_state, json, reduce, scenario};
const P1: PlayerId = PlayerId::P1;
const P2: PlayerId = PlayerId::P2;

#[test]
fn a_second_play_ai_turn_on_the_same_game_applies_every_action_it_returns() {
    jackioh_cards::register_all();
    let start = scenario(json!({
        "seed": "audit-turns", "active": "p1", "turn": 9,
        "p1": { "hand": ["core-025", "core-011"], "mana": 4, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-019"] },
        "p2": { "hand": ["core-025", "core-011"], "mana": 4, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-019"] },
    })).state().clone();
    let mut ai = AiOptions::with_budget(create_rng("audit-turns", 0), AI_GATE_BUDGET);
    let first = play_ai_turn(&start, P1, &mut ai);
    assert!(first.actions.len() >= 2, "p1 plays and ends its turn");
    let second = play_ai_turn(&first.state, P2, &mut ai);

    let mut current = first.state.clone();
    for action in &second.actions {
        let next = reduce(&current, &Action::new(action.body.clone(), P2, action.nonce.clone()));
        assert!(next.error.is_none());
        assert_ne!(hash_state(&next.state), hash_state(&current),
            "p2's action {} ({:?}) changed nothing: its nonce was p1's", action.nonce, action.body);
        current = next.state;
    }
}
```

Output today: ``assertion `left != right` failed: p2's action t0 (Play { instance_id: "c6", … }) changed nothing: its nonce was p1's``.

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/match_.rs`, `play_ai_turn`.

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Make the nonce unique within a game: skip any `t{n}` already in `state.applied`, or number from the game's own count. Skipping keeps `t0, t1, …` for a first call, which a test pins.
- The format is a pinned surface: `docs/polish/3-ai.md` says "nonces `t${n}`", and `crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs` has `plays_decides_actions_with_nonces_t0_t1_until_the_ai_owes_nothing`. Keep both true for a first call, or change both in the same pull request.
- No existing test chains two calls on one game (checked: every caller in `crates/ai/tests` makes one call per state), so nothing else should move.

Found by an audit of the AI crate; the reproduction was run and the code path read before filing.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45489941009)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`play_ai_turn` mints one nonce per action starting at `t0` on every call, so a second call on the same game replays the first turn's nonces: the engine answers them unchanged with `error: None`, and the swallowed decisions are still pushed onto `actions`/`decisions`. Done means every action `play_ai_turn` returns is an action the engine applied, per the `crates/ai/README.md` Matches contract ("`play_ai_turn` plays one AI turn out"), while a first call on a fresh game still mints `t0, t1, …` exactly as `docs/polish/3-ai.md` and the surface test pin it.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/ai/src/match_.rs` | change | `play_ai_turn` (line 488): skip taken `t{n}` nonces; loop bound becomes `actions.len()`; doc comment notes the skip |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs` | change | `mod surface_play_ai_turn`: one new regression test; existing `t0…` pin untouched |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `spec/`, `docs/`, `apps/`, or any crate besides `crates/ai`. Governing sections: engine nonce dedupe (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs` `reduce_held`, `NONCE_HISTORY` in `crates/engine/src/config.rs`), the AI README Matches contract, and the `t${n}` surface in `docs/polish/3-ai.md`. No new ruling: this is a bug against the existing contract plus §9.3 dedupe, not a rules decision the spec leaves open, so no `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/` or `spec/11-rulings.md` change.

## Steps

1. In `play_ai_turn` (`crates/ai/src/match_.rs:488`), keep the overall shape (decide → `Action::new` → `reduce`, break on refusal) and insert a skip before minting, following the precedent of `nonce_for` in `crates/engine/src/subsystems/ai_policy.rs:117`, which also probes `state.applied` for collisions:
   ```rust
   while current.applied.iter().any(|entry| entry.nonce == format!("t{n}")) {
       n += 1;
   }
   let action = Action::new(decision.action.clone(), seat, format!("t{n}"));
   n += 1;
   ```
   Probe `current` (not the input `state`), so nonces minted earlier in the same turn are skipped too.
2. In the same function, change the loop bound from `n < AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS` to `actions.len() < AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS`. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: if skips advanced `n` against the ceiling, a turn following a 60-action turn would skip `t0…t59` and exit without playing. `n` counts nonce suffixes from here on; `actions.len()` counts played actions, which is what the ceiling limits (on a fresh game they coincide, so single-call behavior is unchanged).
3. Update the function's `///` doc line to `decide → reduce until !ai_to_act(state, seat) or AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS; nonces t${n}, skipping any the game already applied`. No constant is added (rule 9: no new numbers; the `t` prefix and ceiling are existing).
4. In `crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs`, inside `mod surface_play_ai_turn` (which already has `jackioh_ai::*` and `testkit::*` in scope), add the issue's reproduction verbatim as `a_second_play_ai_turn_on_the_same_game_applies_every_action_it_returns`: scenario seed `"audit-turns"`, p1's turn via `play_ai_turn(&start, P1, …)`, then `play_ai_turn(&first.state, P2, …)`; fold each of the second turn's actions through `reduce` with `Action::new(action.body.clone(), P2, action.nonce.clone())` and assert `error.is_none()` plus `hash_state` changes. Use `PlayerId::P1/P2` directly (the module's `AI` const is p1-only by the support header's redact convention; this test asserts mechanics, not decision quality).
5. Run the module tests, clippy for the crate, and fmt (exact commands under Tests).

## Tests

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs`, `mod surface_play_ai_turn`: new `a_second_play_ai_turn_on_the_same_game_applies_every_action_it_returns` — fails on `main` (p2's `t0` replays p1's play of `c6`, state unchanged), passes after the fix (every returned action reduces cleanly and changes state).
- Same module: existing `plays_decides_actions_with_nonces_t0_t1_until_the_ai_owes_nothing` — must keep passing, proving a first call still mints exactly `t0, t1, …` with `actions.len() == decisions.len()`.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai surface_play_ai_turn`, then `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. No engine, web, or spec-check runs are needed (no engine/spec/doc files change; signature is unchanged so WASM/TS need nothing).

## Done when

- [ ] A chained second `play_ai_turn` on one game returns only engine-applied actions (new test green, and it fails with the fix reverted)
- [ ] A first call still mints `t0, t1, …` with actions/decisions aligned (existing surface pin green)
- [ ] No other `crates/ai` test needed moving: single-call callers behave exactly as before (skip is a no-op on a fresh `applied`)
- [ ] The three commands above are green

## Risks

- Counting skips against `AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS` would starve a turn following a long turn of its whole ceiling; the `actions.len()` bound in step 2 prevents this — verify by re-reading the loop before running tests.
- Matching only `current.applied` (the last `NONCE_HISTORY` = 64 entries) is exactly the engine's dedupe window, so a `t{n}` evicted from the window is one the engine will treat as new; reuse there is safe by construction, and 60 (the ceiling) < 64, so a full first turn's nonces are all still skipped on the next call.
- Nonce choice derives from state only: deterministic, pure (rule 4 intact), carries no hidden information (rule 7 intact), and the public signature is unchanged, so no caller, WASM binding, or doc needs updating.

## Open questions

- The hard-rule's parenthetical ("The AI … (`crates/ai/src/`)") reads strictly as hard, but the change is a mechanical nonce-minting loop touching neither decisions nor search, so medium stands; flagging per the brief rather than re-rating.
- The duplicate notice (#4799 item 5, same defect): the bot holds no GitHub credential and cannot comment on the other issue, so a person should note there once this lands rather than the builder widening this change to cover it.
````
